proved_step: CLAIMED, kind ALGORITHM (boundary result, does NOT close G0001). Statement: let W in Z^{m x n}, t, v in Z^m, T in Z, and suppose the supports S_1..S_m of the rows of W are pairwise disjoint, |S_j| = k_j. Let c_j = #{y in {0,1}^{S_j} : sum_{i in S_j} W[j,i] y_i >= t_j}. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} = 2^f * sum_{e >= T} [z^e] prod_j ((2^{k_j} - c_j) + c_j z^{v_j}), with f = n - sum_j k_j. Proof: under uniform x, the events E_j = [W_j.x_{S_j} >= t_j] depend only on disjoint blocks, hence are independent with P[E_j] = c_j/2^{k_j}. Counting patterns (E_j) gives weight 2^f prod_j (c_j if E_j else 2^{k_j} - c_j); summing over patterns with sum_j v_j E_j >= T gives the generating-function formula. Running time: O(sum_j 2^{k_j}) to compute the c_j, plus m block updates on a polynomial of at most m*V+1 coefficients (V = max |v_j|). Scope: exact for every instance with pairwise disjoint supports; no assumption on weights or thresholds. Evidence: cm-07270f02ad1441eb (60 random disjoint-block instances, n in {8,10,12}, 0 mismatches vs brute force, EXPLORATORY_COMPUTATION). Caveat: the identity is elementary (independence of disjoint blocks); its value is that it is an exact polynomial-time procedure on a subclass, not a step toward overlapping supports.

evidence: Review by R0806 (not the author). (1) The identity #{x: sum_j v_j[E_j] >= T} = 2^f * sum_{e>=T} [z^e] prod_j((2^{k_j}-c_j)+c_j z^{v_j}) is correct for v_j >= 0 (independence of disjoint blocks, block counts c_j and 2^{k_j}-c_j). (2) As stated, 'no assumption on weights' is false: for v_j < 0, z^{v_j} is a Laurent monomial, so the 'polynomial of at most m*V+1 coefficients' running-time claim does not hold as written. (3) Scope issue: pairwise disjoint nonempty supports force sum_j |S_j| <= n, so at most n bottom gates are non-constant. For m = ceil(n^1.5) the subclass is therefore vacuous for alpha > 1 (all but <= n gates are constant), and it does not meet O1 or O2 for alpha = 1.5. Refutation applies to the stated scope and running-time claim only; the v_j >= 0 identity itself stands.

lemma: Repair of S0002 (CLAIMED, not yet reviewed). For integer v_j, write v_j E_j = v_j + |v_j|(1-E_j) when v_j<0, where 1-E_j = [W_j.x < t_j] is again a threshold event of block S_j with c'_j = 2^{k_j} - c_j satisfying the same independence. Then sum_j v_j E_j >= T iff sum_{j: v_j>0} v_j E_j + sum_{j: v_j<0} |v_j| F_j >= T - V_neg, where V_neg = sum_{v_j<0} v_j and F_j = 1-E_j. The right side is a nonnegative-weight generating function with coefficients on 0..(sum |v_j|), so the count is 2^f * sum_{e >= T - V_neg} [z^e] prod_j (block factor), polynomial in m*V with V = max |v_j|. Scope: pairwise disjoint supports; this does NOT close G0001 because disjointness forces at most n non-constant bottom gates, so for m = n^1.5 it covers only gates that are constant. Its use is as a building block (e.g. for blocks of bounded overlap), which is not yet proved.

proved_step: CLAIMED, kind ALGORITHM (addresses G0001; closure not claimed, pending independent review). Setting: f(x) = [sum_j v_j [sum_{i in S_j} w_{ji} x_i >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n, with |S_j| <= k, each variable in at most D supports S_j, m gates, V = max |v_j|. Claim: #f can be computed exactly in time poly(n, m, V) * 2^{n - n/(Dk+1)}. Proof: fix an order of variables; let A_p be the set of variables at positions <= p that lie in some S_j containing a variable at a position > p. Each gate touching A_p contains a suffix variable, so |A_p| <= min(p, Dk(n-p)), and max_p min(p, a(n-p)) = n - n/(a+1) for a = Dk. Dynamic program over p: state = assignment to A_p, value = polynomial in z whose exponent is the sum of v_j over gates already decided. A gate with last position p is determined by the state at step p, since its earlier variables lie in A_{p-1}. Exactness is by induction on p. Time: sum_p 2^{|A_p|} * (2mV+1) * m * 2^k. Scope: all instances with fan-in <= k and max variable degree <= D; weights and thresholds arbitrary. Consequence: for m = n^alpha, alpha < 2, fixed k, D = C n^{alpha-1}, the saving is 2^{Omega(n^{2-alpha})}, superpolynomial, so 2^n / n^{omega(1)} for that subclass. Evidence: cm-7f058b7dae1d4e23 (60 random instances, n in {8,10,12,14}, k in {2,3}; 0 brute mismatches, 0 frontier-bound violations). The exponent itself is not measured; it is a bound.

proved_step: CLAIMED, kind ALGORITHM (sub-case, does NOT close G0001). Statement: let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T] on {0,1}^n with integer W, t, v, T and m rows, and let U = union of supp(W_j) over all j with |U| = s. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} = 2^(n-s) * #{y in {0,1}^U : f(y)=1}, and the right-hand count is computed in time O(2^s * m * s) by enumerating y in {0,1}^U and evaluating each gate. Proof: for each j, W_j . x = W_j|_U . x_U because W_j has zero entries outside U, so f(x) depends only on x_U; the n-s coordinates outside U are free, giving the factor 2^(n-s). The enumeration evaluates m gates of support <= s at each of the 2^s points. Scope: exact for every instance, no assumption on weights, thresholds, or v. Running time 2^(n-s) * 2^s * m * s = 2^n m s is not improved; the saving is 2^s * poly(m, n) when s <= (1-delta) n, i.e. 2^{(1-delta) n} poly. Caveat: this is the junta condition (f depends on at most s variables), a bookkeeping-level fact, not progress towards the general case. For the target size m = n^1.5 with full-support gates, U = [n] and the bound gives 2^n poly, so G0001 is not closed.

proved_step: LEMMA-DIR (repair of S0002 for G0001). Setting: n >= 1, B >= 1, D >= 1. Directions a_1..a_D in Z^n with |a_{d,i}| <= B. Gates j = 1..m, each with direction d(j), threshold t_j in Z, weight v_j in Z. Threshold T in Z. Let N(F) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [a_{d(j)} . x >= t_j] >= T}. CLAIM: N(F) is computed exactly in O(n (2Bn+1)^D (D+m)) arithmetic operations on integers of O(n + log(m B)) bits. PROOF: Let Y(x) = (a_1.x, ..., a_D.x) in Z^D and N_y = #{x : Y(x) = y}. Then N(F) = sum over y of N_y [g(y) >= T], where g(y) = sum_j v_j [y_{d(j)} >= t_j]. Let N^(i)_y count the prefixes x_1..x_i with partial sums y. Recursion: N^(i)_y = N^(i-1)_y + N^(i-1)_{y - c_i}, where c_i = (a_{1,i}, ..., a_{D,i}), because x_i in {0,1}. N^(0) is the point mass at 0. The support of N^(i) lies in the box [-iB, iB]^D, which has at most (2iB+1)^D <= (2Bn+1)^D points. Each step costs at most (2Bn+1)^D D operations. Evaluating g at each of these points costs O(m) naively. The total is therefore O(n (2Bn+1)^D (D+m)). COROLLARY (the subclass): if D <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bn+1), then (2Bn+1)^D <= 2^{(1-delta) n}, so the running time is 2^{(1-delta) n} times n^{O(1)}, and this holds for every m = poly(n), including m = n^alpha for any alpha > 1. For B = poly(n), the condition reads D <= (1-delta') n / log n. The subclass is defined by few distinct weight vectors, not by disjoint supports, so it allows overlapping supports and m > n. SCOPE: the subclass only. It does not cover D = Theta(n) distinct directions, and it is not a general #SAT algorithm.

proved_step: CLAIMED: Setting: W integer m x n, t and v integer vectors, T integer, all entries bounded by M, rank_Q(W) = r. Claim: the count #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed exactly in time (2nM+1)^r times (n+m) times r times poly(log(nM)) by a dynamic program. Proof: pick r linearly independent rows B_1..B_r of W and columns S with B_S (r x r) nonsingular; Delta = det(B_S) != 0 and |Delta| <= r^(r/2) M^r. Each row satisfies W_j = c_j B with c_j = W_j|_S B_S^{-1}, so a_j = Delta c_j = W_j|_S adj(B_S) is an integer vector. Let z(x) = Bx in Z^r. Then W_j.x = c_j.z(x), so W_j.x >= t_j iff a_j.z(x) >= Delta t_j (flip the inequality if Delta < 0). The DP processes variables 1..n; its state is the partial sum z_p = sum_{i<=p} x_i B_{.,i} with a multiplicity. Every coordinate of z_p has absolute value <= nM, so there are at most (2nM+1)^r states. At the end each state's top value is computed from the gates and the counts with value >= T are summed. Consequence: if r <= n / (4 log2(2nM+1)) and M <= n^O(1), the running time is 2^(n/4) times poly(n,m), which is 2^n / n^omega(1). Scope: only low-rank W (rank r with r log n = O(n)); random W has rank n and is not covered. Evidence: cm-9d2f09f8562c4e75 (exploratory: 300 random low-rank instances, 0 mismatches; max states 392 at rank 2, n=32; 5092 at rank 3, n=32). Needs independent review: the DP correctness, the state bound, and whether this discharges G0001 as recorded.

proved_step: LEMMA-WIN (window / bandwidth DP, ALGORITHM). Setting: C(x) = sum_{j=1}^m v_j [w_j . x_{I_j} >= t_j], integer v_j, t_j, w_j, where each bottom gate has support in a window I_j = [a_j, a_j + L_j - 1] of length L_j <= L (x in {0,1}^n, n >= 1). Let S = sum_j |v_j|. Claim: #{x : C(x) >= T} is computed exactly in time O(2^L (2S+1) (n + m L)). PROOF. Process bits x_0, ..., x_{n-1} in order. State after reading x_0..x_i: (mask, s), where mask = (x_{i-L+1}, ..., x_i) (padded with 0 for indices < 0) and s = sum of v_j over gates with end e_j = a_j + L_j - 1 <= i whose threshold event holds. Invariant: for a gate with e_j = i, its window [a_j, e_j] has length L_j <= L, so [a_j, e_j] is contained in [i-L+1, i] and its event is a function of mask alone; hence the transition (mask, s) -> (mask', s') with mask' = ((mask << 1) | b) mod 2^L and s' = s + sum of v_j over gates with e_j = i+1 that fire is well defined. Gates are evaluated at their end step, so the DP state carries everything needed: its value at step i is the number of prefixes with that (mask, s). Summing counts over states with s >= T at step n-1 gives the exact count (each full x is one path). Cost: at most 2^L states per step times 2S+1 sum values; each gate is evaluated once per state (cost L_j) and transitions cost O(1) per gate evaluation after precomputing. Total O(n 2^L (2S+1)) plus O(m L 2^L (2S+1)) for gate evaluations, which is O(2^L (2S+1)(n + mL)). COROLLARY. Let s(n) = omega(log n) and L = n - s(n). For the subclass of size m = n^alpha with V = max|v_j| constant (so S <= m V = poly(n)) and span(support of each bottom gate) <= L, the count runs in 2^{n - s(n)} poly(n) = 2^n / n^{omega(1)} time, since 2^{s(n)} = n^{omega(1)}. SCOPE: (i) exact #SAT only, not CAPP; (ii) subclass only: random integer bottom gates have full support (span n-1) with high probability, so the subclass excludes generic instances; (iii) no lower bound transfer is claimed. Evidence for correctness: cm-5c396888cfee4f4a (440 random window instances, n in {6,8,10,12}, 0 mismatches against brute force). Repairs still needed: the generic class (G0007 / G0002), and a proof that the window subclass is not trivial relative to the owner's size target.

proved_step: LEMMA-ARR (CLAIMED, scope: m bottom gates, any n). For integer W in Z^{m x n}, t in Z^m, the number of distinct patterns P(x) = ([W_j.x >= t_j])_j over x in {0,1}^n is at most sum_{i=0}^{n} C(m,i) <= (e m / n)^n. Proof: [W_j.x >= t_j] iff W_j.x > t_j - 1/2 for integer x, so P(x) is the sign vector of x with respect to the m affine hyperplanes H_j = {y : W_j.y = t_j - 1/2} in R^n. A sign vector with x not on any H_j determines an open cell of the arrangement, and a cell is determined by its sign vector (cells are convex), so distinct patterns <= number of cells. Buck (1943) / Cover (1965): an arrangement of m hyperplanes in R^n has at most sum_{i<=n} C(m,i) regions. Consequence: for m <= n/4, patterns <= (e/4)^n <= 2^{0.56 n}, i.e. delta = 0.44. Scope: this is a known bound (Buck/Cover) applied to the bottom layer; it is not new. It does NOT close G0001: for m = n^alpha with alpha > 1 the bound is at least 2^n, and no algorithm enumerating the realised patterns in 2^{(1-delta)n} time is given.

refuted_approach: LEMMA-ARR consequence was wrong: for m <= n/4 the bound (e/4)^n is below 1. Correct bound: distinct patterns <= min(2^m, sum_{i<=n} C(m,i)); for m <= n it is 2^m, so m <= (1-delta)n gives 2^{(1-delta)n}. For m >= n the bound is never below the trivial 2^n, so it does not apply to m = n^alpha, alpha > 1.

proved_step: ALG-FEWDIR (CLAIMED, scope: THR o THR circuits C(x) = [sum_j v_j [<W_j,x> >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n, where all bottom weight vectors W_j in Z^n take at most D distinct values d_1..d_D, and |entries| <= B. Claim: #C = #{x : C(x)=1} is computed exactly in O(n * m * D * (2nB+1)^D) arithmetic operations. Proof: (i) For x, let s(x) = (<d_1,x>,...,<d_D,x>) in Z^D. Every bottom gate equals [s_{g(j)}(x) >= t_j] for its direction index g(j), so C(x) is a function F(s(x)) with F(s) = [sum_j v_j [s_{g(j)} >= t_j] >= T]. (ii) Dynamic programming: after processing variables x_1..x_i, let N_i(s) = #{(x_1..x_i) : s(x_1..x_i)=s}. Then N_0 = {0:1} and N_{i} is obtained from N_{i-1} by adding 0 or d_{1,i},...,d_{D,i} to each state, which is exact by induction. (iii) #C = sum_{s} N_n(s) F(s). (iv) Each coordinate of s(x) lies in [-nB, nB], so at most (2nB+1)^D states exist at every step. Each step does at most 2 * (2nB+1)^D updates of O(D) work, and evaluating F on a state costs O(m). Total O(n (2nB+1)^D (D + m)). Consequence: for D <= c log n and B <= n^k, the time is 2^{O(log^2 n)} * poly(n), hence 2^n / n^{omega(1)} for this subclass. Scope: a subclass of THR o THR where the number of distinct bottom directions is O(log n). This is a proof for the subclass only. For general m = n^alpha the number of distinct directions can be m, and the bound becomes 2^{Omega(n^{c})}. It does NOT close G0001 or G0007. The result is a standard counting argument, not new; its use is as an O2 subclass theorem.

proved_step: LEMMA-WIN (subclass: interval supports of length <= L in a fixed order). Setting: f(x) = [sum_j v_j [sum_k w_{j,k} x_{a_j+k} >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n, m gates, gate j has support I_j = [a_j, a_j+l_j-1] with l_j <= L, integer weights |w| <= B, |v_j| <= V. PROOF: left-to-right DP. State after position i = (last L-1 bits of x_1..x_i, partial sum s in [-mV, mV]) with a count. At position i, for each state and each new bit b, the window (last L-1 bits, b) contains x_{a_j..i} for every gate j with I_j ending at i (length l_j <= L). Evaluate e_j = [w_j . window >= t_j], add v_j e_j to s, and keep the last L-1 bits. Each assignment x corresponds to exactly one DP path, and each gate's value depends only on x restricted to I_j, which is in the window when the gate is processed, so the final sum over states with s >= T is exactly #f. TIME: n positions x 2^{L-1} keys x (2mV+1) sums x 2 bits x (gates ending here, <= m) x L work = O(n m^2 L V 2^L) arithmetic. For L = (1-delta) n and m, V, B = poly(n) this is 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n) = 2^n / n^{omega(1)}; for L = O(log n) it is polynomial. SCOPE: interval supports in one fixed order only; not general THR o THR. STATUS: CLAIMED, not reviewed. Risk: the reviewer may judge it the standard bandwidth/path-decomposition DP, which would not count as progress under the owner's criterion.

proved_step: PROCEDURE (path-order DP, CLAIMED, unreviewed). Setting: g_j(x)=[sum_{u in S_j} w_{j,u} x_u >= t_j], |S_j|<=k, integer weights, top weights v_j with |v_j|<=V, threshold T, m gates. Fix a linear order pi on [n]; for each position i let A_i = {u <=_pi i : u in S_j for some j with max_pi S_j >_pi i} and w(pi)=max_i |A_i|. Then N = #{x: sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T} is computed exactly in time O(n 2^{w(pi)} (2mV+1) mk). Proof: DP table D_i indexed by (a in {0,1}^{A_i}, s in [-mV,mV]) with invariant c = #{y in {0,1}^{<=i}: y|_{A_i}=a, sigma_i(y)=s}, where sigma_i(y) = sum over gates with max S_j <= i of v_j g_j(y_{S_j}). Base D_{-1}={(empty,0):1}. Step: a gate with max S_j=i has support inside A_{i-1} union {i} (any u<i in S_j has max S_j > i-1, so u in A_{i-1}), so its contribution depends only on (a', b) with b = y_i; hence D_i is a function of D_{i-1}. At the end A_{n-1} is empty and the answer is sum_{s>=T} D_{n-1}(empty,s). Table size per step is at most 2^w (2mV+1). Qed. Scope: an exact procedure parameterised by w(pi). It is the standard path-decomposition DP, so a reviewer may judge it trivial. It does NOT close G0002, because G0002 also needs pw <= (1-delta) n for a stated subclass of size n^alpha, which is not proved. Full-support gates force w = n-1 under the identity order.

lemma: BOUNDARY DP (repair of G0002, construction half only). Fix a THR o THR circuit f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on n variables, and an ordering pi of the variables. For a prefix P_k = {pi_1..pi_k} let B_k = the placed variables that lie in some bottom gate whose support is not inside P_k. Claim: #{x : f(x)=1} is computed exactly by a DP over the states (a|B_k, s_k), where a|B_k is the assignment to B_k and s_k = sum over bottom gates completed by P_k of v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] (an integer in [-V, V], V = sum |v_j|). Proof: for any completion y of the unplaced variables, the still-open gates j have W_j.x = W_j.(a|B_k, y) + const, so their values depend only on a|B_k; completed gates contribute only through s_k. Two prefixes with equal (a|B_k, s_k) therefore have identical completion counts, which justifies the merge. Hence the count is exact and the running time is n * max_k 2^{|B_k|} * (2V+1) * poly(m). Scope: a bound on time for a class needs a bound on max_k |B_k| for ALL instances in the class.

lemma: Clipped-State DP for THR∘THR #SAT. Let C be a THR∘THR circuit on n variables with m = n^α bottom gates (α > 0). Split variables into X_A (first a = ⌊n/2⌋) and X_B (rest). For each bottom gate j, let W^A_j, W^B_j be its weights on X_A, X_B; threshold t_j. Define lo_j = min_{x_B} W^B_j·x_B, hi_j = max_{x_B} W^B_j·x_B. For x_A ∈ {0,1}^a, the clipped vector c(x_A) ∈ ℤ^m has entries c_j = clip(t_j - W^A_j·x_A, lo_j, hi_j + 1). Then #SAT(C) = Σ_{c ∈ C} |{x_A : c(x_A) = c}| · R(c), where R(c) = |{x_B : (W^B_j·x_B ≥ c_j for all j) is satisfied and the top threshold holds}|. The number of distinct clip vectors K_clip ≤ Π_j (|{W^B_j·x_B : x_B ∈ {0,1}^b}| + 2).
gap: Need to analyze K_clip scaling for random/mixed weight classes. Does K_clip = 2^{o(n)} for some natural subclass (e.g., bounded weights, low rank, restricted top fan-in)?
proved_step: Lemma statement recorded. Next: prove the exactness (counting identity) and bound K_clip. The identity holds because for fixed x_A, the condition W_j·x ≥ t_j is equivalent to W^B_j·x_B ≥ t_j - W^A_j·x_A. Since W^B_j·x_B ∈ [lo_j, hi_j], values below lo_j are always true (so clip to lo_j), values above hi_j are always false (so clip to hi_j+1 as an impossible threshold). Thus the condition depends on x_A only through c(x_A). Summing over c gives the exact count. The bound on K_clip follows because each c_j takes at most |supp_B(j)| + 2 values.

lemma: SUBCLASS DP (exact, proved). Let C = THR o THR with n Boolean inputs, m bottom gates [W_j.x >= t_j], integer weights 0 <= W_j,i <= B, top weights v_j and threshold T. Suppose the m weight vectors take at most c distinct values (as vectors, indexed by inv(j)). Then #{x : C(x)=1} is computed by the layered DP over states s in [0, Bn]^c (s_d = W_d . x_{<i} after i variables) in time O(n * m * min(2^n, (Bn+1)^c)) arithmetic operations. Proof: after reading x_0..x_{i-1} define s(x_{<i}) in [0,Bn]^c. Each bottom gate value [W_j.x >= t_j] is a function of s_{inv(j)} at the end, and the step x_i -> s + b*W_{.,i} is a deterministic map on states. So the map x -> s(x) is a function from {0,1}^n to states that commutes with each step; the count of x with s(x)=s equals the DP count (induction on i). C(x) depends only on s(x) at i=n, so #C = sum over final states s satisfying the top predicate of the DP count. Each layer has at most min(2^i, (Bn+1)^c) states.

proved_step: REPAIR-S (candidate, CLAIMED). Setting: C(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, integer W, t, v, T. Split variables into A and B with |A| = a, |B| = b = n - a. For x_A, let u_j(x_A) = sum_{i in A} W_ji x_i, and let lo_j = sum_{i in B} min(W_ji, 0), hi_j = sum_{i in B} max(W_ji, 0). Let c_j(x_A) = clip(t_j - u_j(x_A), lo_j, hi_j + 1) and c(x_A) = (c_j). (a) EXACT IDENTITY: #C = sum over distinct vectors c of |{x_A : c(x_A) = c}| * R(c), where R(c) = #{x_B : sum_j v_j [W^B_j.x_B >= c_j] >= T}. Proof: bottom gate j fires iff W^B_j.x_B >= t_j - u_j. Since W^B_j.x_B lies in [lo_j, hi_j], replacing t_j - u_j by its clip to [lo_j, hi_j+1] leaves the predicate unchanged for every x_B: if t_j - u_j < lo_j both sides are always true, if t_j - u_j > hi_j both are always false, and otherwise the clip is the identity. So the fire pattern depends only on c(x_A). (b) K-BOUND: let K = number of distinct c(x_A). Then K <= prod_j min(N_j, hi_j - lo_j + 2), where N_j = number of distinct values u_j(x_A) <= 2^{|S_j cap A|}, and S_j is the support of W_j. Proof: c_j is a function of u_j alone, so c(x_A) lies in the product of the images of the c_j; the image of c_j has at most N_j elements and lies in the integer interval [lo_j, hi_j+1]. Hence K <= prod_j min(N_j, hi_j - lo_j + 2) <= 2^{sigma(A)} with sigma(A) = sum_j min(|S_j cap A|, L_j), L_j = ceil(log2(hi_j - lo_j + 2)). (c) TIME: the algorithm (enumerate x_A, group by c, compute R(c) by enumerating x_B) runs in poly(n,m) * (2^a + 2^{sigma(A)+b}). COROLLARY (a subclass, stated exactly): let max |W_ji| <= Bw and L = ceil(log2(n Bw + 2)). If for some B of size delta*n, sum_j min(|S_j minus B|, L) <= (1 - 2 delta) n, then with a = (1-delta) n, #SAT of C is computed in poly(n,m) * 2^{(1-delta) n} time. Scope: this is a repair of the refuted lemma (the old bound K_clip * 2^{n/2} is replaced by the per-gate bound, which is not bounded by 2^{n/2}); it does NOT close G0001 or G0007 for the general class; the regime m*L <= (1-2 delta) n is already covered by LEMMA-DIR; the new content is the case where most gates live on a delta*n core B.

lemma: CUTWIDTH DP (subclass, exact). Let C = THR o THR on n Boolean inputs with m bottom gates [W_j.x >= t_j], integer weights 0 <= W_{j,i} <= B, supports S_j, top weights v_j, threshold T. Fix a variable order 0..n-1 and let a_i = #{j : some variable of S_j lies below i and some lies at or above i} (gates active at cut i). Then #{x : C(x)=1} is computed by a layered DP whose state after reading x_0..x_{i-1} is (number of completed gates whose value is 1, partial sums of the active gates). Partial sums of an active gate lie in [0, B s], so the layer has at most (m+1)(Bs+1)^{a_i} states, and the total work is at most 2n(m+1) max_i (Bs+1)^{a_i}. Correctness: the final value of each gate depends on its partial sum at cut i plus contributions from x_{>=i}, so the state is a sufficient statistic and the DP counts are exact by induction on i. Consequence: if a_i <= (1-delta) n / log2(Bs+1) for all i, #C is computed in 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n) time. This recovers the box bound for m <= (1-delta)n/log2(Bs+1) as the special case a_i = m.
gap: Does NOT close G0001 or G0002. For random supports with m = n^{1.5} gates the cut width a_i = Theta(m) at the middle cut, so the bound needs m = O(n/log n), far below n^alpha for alpha > 1. proved_step: BANDWIDTH WINDOW DP (subclass, exact, O2). Let C(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, with integer W_{j,k} >= 0, integer t_j, integer v_j >= 0, V = sum_j v_j, and S_j = supp(W_j). Bandwidth b: for every bottom gate j, max S_j - min S_j <= b. Let first_j = min S_j and last_j = max S_j. CLAIM: #{x : C(x)=1} is computed exactly with O((V+1) 2^b poly(n,m)) operations. PROOF. Read x_0,...,x_{n-1} in order. After reading x_0..x_{i-1}, the state is (u, sigma): u = sum of v_j over gates with last_j < i and value 1; sigma_j = sum over k in S_j, k < i, of W_{j,k} x_k for each gate with first_j < i <= last_j (active); sigma_j = 0 for gates with first_j >= i. Keep counts N_i(u, sigma) of prefixes. SUFFICIENCY: finished gates are already fixed in u; each active gate's final value is [sigma_j + sum over k in S_j, k >= i of W_{j,k} x_k >= t_j], which depends only on sigma_j and the suffix. So the number of completions with C = 1 depends only on (u, sigma), and the layer-to-layer transition is exact by induction; at i = n, C = [u >= T]. WINDOW: for an active gate, last_j >= i and last_j - first_j <= b give first_j >= i - b, so sigma_j is a function of x_{i-b}..x_{i-1}. Hence sigma takes at most 2^b values and each layer has at most (V+1) 2^b states. CONSEQUENCE: for b <= (1-delta) n the count takes 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n, m) time (V poly-bounded). NON-VACUITY: for every alpha the class contains circuits of size n^alpha (supports inside windows of length n/2, many distinct gates available), so this is a proved running time for a subclass of size n^alpha. Weights W are not restricted in size; only the number of distinct sigma values matters.

lemma: FEW-FORMS DP: if the bottom weight rows of a THR o THR circuit take r distinct values in Z^n with entries bounded by B, then #SAT is exact in O(n(m+r)(2Bn+1)^r) time by a DP over the r partial sums; for r <= n/(2 log2(2Bn+1)) and constant B this is 2^{n/2} poly(n).

proved_step: Factorisation C(x) = G(s(x)) with s(x) = (<f_k,x>)_k in Z^r; path-count recurrence N_i(sigma) = N_{i-1}(sigma) + N_{i-1}(sigma - c_i) with c_i the i-th column of the r distinct forms, giving #C = sum_sigma N_n(sigma) G(sigma); range supp N_i in [-Bi,Bi]^r gives at most (2Bn+1)^r states; n steps and O(m+r) per final state. Full proof in the session record.

proved_step: LEMMA (unit weights, any threshold, session R0856). Let g(x)=[sum_{i in S} x_i >= t], |S|=s, t any integer. Let rho leave each variable free with probability q <= 1/4 and otherwise fix it to 0 or 1 with probability 1/2 each. Then Pr_rho[g|rho non-constant] <= sqrt(2)*q*sqrt(s) + exp(-s/8). PROOF: let F = number of free vars in S, k = s-F. Given F, f1 (number fixed to 1) ~ Bin(k,1/2) and g|rho is non-constant iff t-F <= f1 <= t-1, which is F consecutive values, so Pr[nonconst | F] <= min(1, F * max_j Pr[Bin(k,1/2)=j]) <= min(1, F/sqrt(k)) using max pmf <= 1/sqrt(k). On {F <= s/2}, k >= s/2 so the term is <= sqrt(2) F / sqrt(s), and E[F] = qs gives <= sqrt(2) q sqrt(s). Pr[F > s/2] <= exp(-2s(1/2-q)^2) <= exp(-s/8) for q <= 1/4 (Hoeffding). Per-gate bound: overlapping supports allowed, union bound over m gates. Weighted gates NOT covered.

lemma: BANDWIDTH-DP. Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n Boolean variables with m bottom gates g_j(x) = [sum_{k in S_j} c_{jk} x_k >= t_j], where every support S_j lies in an interval of length at most w-1 (max S_j - min S_j <= w-1), |c_{jk}| <= B, integer top weights v_j, R = sum_j |v_j|, top threshold T. Then N(C) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T} is computed exactly by a dynamic program over variables 0..n-1 whose states are (window pattern, partial top sum), with at most 2^(w-1)(2R+1) states per step, in O(2^(w-1)(2R+1)(n + m w)) operations. For w <= (1-delta)n and R <= poly(n), this gives 2^((1-delta)n) poly(n,m) time for this subclass (the second alternative of obligation O1).
evidence: cm-3d1392ee358847e0 (EXPLORATORY_COMPUTATION, sanity check, not a proof): 400 random instances, n in [2,9], random bandwidth w, m <= 6 gates with spans <= w-1; DP count equals brute force on all 400 (0 mismatches); state count never exceeds 2^(w-1)(2R+1) (max ratio 1.0). This is a finite check of the code, not evidence for the general claim.
proved_step: PROOF. Order variables 0..n-1. Let i be the step after x_i is assigned. Define pi_i = (x_k for k in [i-w+2, i]) (at most w-1 bits) and A_i = A_0 + sum over gates j with max S_j <= i of v_j g_j(x), where A_0 = sum of v_j over constant gates (S_j empty) that are true. Transition: a gate j with max S_j = i has S_j contained in [i-w+1, i], and pi_{i-1} covers [i-w+1, i-1] together with x_i, so g_j is determined by (pi_{i-1}, x_i). Every gate finalized at a step i' > i has min S_j >= i'-w+1 >= i+2-w, so its variables are kept in pi_i. Hence the successor of state (pi_{i-1}, A_{i-1}) under x_i depends only on that state and x_i, and the number of extensions of a state equals the number of x-prefixes mapping to it. By induction the DP's accumulated count per state equals the number of prefixes x_0..x_i with that state, and N(C) = sum of counts over final states with A_{n-1} >= T. STATE BOUND: |pi_i| <= 2^(w-1). Each v_j enters A at most once, so A_i lies in [-R, R] (since A_0 is a subset sum of the v_j) and takes at most 2R+1 values. Hence states <= 2^(w-1)(2R+1). Per step, each state branches twice, and evaluating the gates finalized at step i costs O(w) each; summing gives the stated operation count. SCOPE: the proof needs every bottom gate to have span <= w-1. Random THR o THR with full supports (span ~ n) are NOT in this subclass for w < n; so the result is a subclass result only. It does not reach n^alpha-size general THR o THR for alpha > 1 without a bandwidth or pathwidth bound on the instance.

lemma: Exact residual state (bookkeeping, not progress). For a THR o THR circuit C = sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T and a prefix rho in {0,1}^i, let dec(rho) = sum of v_j over gates with s_j - R_j^{(i)} >= t_j (s_j = W_j,prefix . rho, R_j^{(i)} = sum_{k>=i} |W_jk|), and und(rho) = {(j, t_j - s_j) : s_j - R_j < t_j <= s_j + R_j}. Then for every suffix y, C(rho,y) = 1 iff sum_{(j,need) in und(rho)} v_j [W_j,suffix . y >= need] >= T - dec(rho). So C|rho is determined by the pair (T - dec(rho), und(rho)), and the number of distinct residual functions K_i <= number of distinct such pairs.
gap: OPEN repair of G0001 via the residual-function state: the measurement shows K_i < 2^i at n=10, but no proof that K_i <= 2^{(1-delta)i} (or that sum_i K_i 2^{n-i} poly(m) <= 2^{(1-delta)n}) for m = n^1.5 random THR gates at growing n. The key is not compressed (keys = 2^i up to i=9), so the compression must come from the und-list collapsing to few distinct threshold patterns; this is the lane S Q-cc869fd7f8 obstacle again, not yet resolved.

proved_step: PROOF. Read x_0, ..., x_{n-1} in order. After reading x_0..x_{k-1} define the window sigma_k = (x_{k-w+1}, ..., x_{k-1}) (indices < 0 read as 0; 2^(w-1) possibilities) and the partial top sum P_k = sum over j with max S_j < k of v_j g_j(x). Each gate with max S_j = k has S_j inside [k-w+1, k], so g_j(x) is a function of (sigma_k, x_k): the transition P_{k+1} = P_k + sum_{j: max S_j = k} v_j g_j(sigma_k, x_k), sigma_{k+1} = last w-1 bits of (sigma_k, x_k) is well defined. Induction on k: the number of completions of a prefix that give top sum >= T depends only on (sigma_k, P_k), since later gates read only the window and later variables. Hence the DP over keys (sigma, P) with counts is exact. |P_k| <= R, so at most 2^(w-1)(2R+1) keys per step, and each step costs O(keys * (2 + m w)). Final answer: sum of counts over keys with P_n >= T. COROLLARY: if w <= (1-delta) n and R <= poly(n), time is 2^((1-delta) n) poly(n, m) on this subclass. Scope: the subclass requires every bottom support to lie in a window of length (1-delta) n under a fixed variable order; generic random supports of size Theta(n) fall outside it.

refuted_approach: Enriched variant of BANDWIDTH-DP (S0079): run the same window/path DP under the best variable order found by 300 random restarts plus 1500 hill-climbing swaps, on random THR o THR instances (m = ceil(n^1.5), supports from weights in {-2..2}, n in {10,12,14}, 3 seeds each). Vertex separation (the DP state measure) is n-1 for every instance and every order tried, so the DP gives no 2^{(1-delta)n} bound on generic random supports. The bandwidth route therefore applies only to subclasses whose supports already lie in a window of width (1-delta)n under a fixed order; it does not reach random THR o THR of size n^alpha.

proved_step: S-BANDWIDTH: Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n variables with m bottom gates g_j(x)=[sum_{k in S_j} c_jk x_k >= t_j], where each support S_j is an interval with max S_j - min S_j <= w-1, |c_jk| <= B, integer top weights v_j, R = sum_j |v_j|, top threshold T. Then N(C) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T} is computed exactly by a DP over variables 0..n-1 whose state after step k is (the last min(k+1, w-1) bits of x, partial top sum s in [-R,R]). The number of states is at most 2^(w-1)(2R+1) and the total time is O(2^(w-1)(2R+1)(n + m w)). Proof: a gate with max S_j = k is evaluated at step k from the window bits, which cover S_j because its width is at most w-1 back from k. A future gate with max S_j = k' > k has min S_j >= k'-w+1 >= k-w+2, so it reads only positions inside the window; the window and partial sum are therefore a sufficient statistic. Consequence: for w <= (1-delta)n and R <= poly(n) (e.g. m = n^alpha, |v_j| <= poly(n)), N(C) is computed in 2^((1-delta)n) poly(n) time. Scope: interval-support subclass only. General overlapping supports (G0001, G0007) are untouched. Caveat: a reviewer may judge this a standard bounded-bandwidth DP, which would mean it does not count as progress under the owner's criterion.

refuted_approach: G0007 candidate form: for a bottom gate on k variables under a random restriction leaving each variable free with probability p, Pr[gate non-constant] <= exp(-c k). Refuted for majority gates (sum_{i in S} x_i >= (k+1)/2): at p = 1/2 the non-constant probability is 0.859, 0.965, 0.997, 0.99998, 0.9999999986 for k = 8..128; at p = 1/8 it is 0.27, 0.38, 0.52, 0.68, 0.84. refuted_approach: G0007 candidate form in its natural use (a positive fraction of bottom gates becomes constant under a restriction that leaves a linear fraction of the variables free) is FALSE for gates of support size k = Theta(n). For unit-weight majority gates with each variable free with probability p fixed (p = 1/2, 1/8), Pr[nonconstant] rises to 1 as k grows (p=1/2: 0.859, 0.965, 0.997, 0.99998, 0.9999999986 for k = 8..128). For k = n^alpha with alpha > 1 this means only about sqrt(k) free variables per gate survive, so a constant-gate lemma needs a restriction that fixes all but about sqrt(n) variables. That is a different restriction regime from the one G0007 names.

proved_step: CLAIMED LEMMA (kind LEMMA, does NOT close G0007): Let M_k(x) = [sum_{i in S} x_i >= t], |S| = k, t = floor((k+1)/2), and let a random restriction keep each variable free independently with probability p, fixing each other variable to a uniform bit. Then Pr[M_k nonconstant] = sum_{f=1}^{k} P(Bin(k,p)=f) * P(t-f <= Bin(k-f,1/2) <= t-1). Since the window {t-f,...,t-1} has f points and max_j P(Bin(m,1/2)=j) <= sqrt(2/(pi m))(1+o(1)), we get Pr <= E[f] sqrt(2/(pi(k-f))) = sqrt(2/pi) p sqrt(k) (1+o(1)) + tail, where the tail is controlled by Chernoff for f > k/2. Asymptotic sharpness: as p sqrt(k) -> 0, Pr / (p sqrt(k)) -> sqrt(2/pi) (only f = 1 contributes at first order). Scope: unit-weight majority only; the general-weight case needs a Littlewood-Offord anti-concentration bound and is open. The proof of the tail term is sketched, not written out, so this is CLAIMED until a second session checks it.

At p=0.1: k=2 about 0.05-0.08, k=3 about 0.06-0.09, k=4 about 0.09-0.12, noisy and not monotone in k. Larger support gives a HIGHER non-constant probability, so the exponential decay in |S_j| does not hold in this family.

proved_step: CLAIMED LEMMA (kind LEMMA; closes only the tail gap G0051(i), not G0007). Setting: k >= 4, S a set of k variables, t = floor((k+1)/2), M(x) = [sum_{i in S} x_i >= t]. A random restriction keeps each variable of S free independently with probability p in [0,1] and fixes the others to uniform bits. Claim: Pr[M|rho nonconstant] <= (2/sqrt(pi)) sqrt(k/(k-2)) p sqrt(k) + (4p)^{k/2}. PROOF. Let F ~ Bin(k,p) be the number of free variables in S. Given F = f, the fixed part has m = k-f variables and sum s ~ Bin(m,1/2). M|rho is nonconstant iff s <= t-1 and s+f >= t, i.e. s in the window [t-f, t-1], which has f integers. So W_f := Pr[nonconstant | F=f] <= f * max_j P(Bin(m,1/2)=j). (a) Max-pmf bound: for m >= 2, max_j P(Bin(m,1/2)=j) <= sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))). Proof: C(2r,r)/4^r <= 1/sqrt(pi r) for r >= 1 (standard). If m = 2r, the max is C(2r,r)/4^r <= sqrt(2/(pi m)) <= sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))). If m = 2r+1, the max is C(2r,r)/4^r * (2r+1)/(2r+2) <= 1/sqrt(pi r) = sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))). (b) Part f <= k/2: then m >= k/2 >= 2 and m-1 >= (k-2)/2, so W_f <= 2f/sqrt(pi(k-2)). Summing with E[F] = kp gives sum_{f<=k/2} P(F=f) W_f <= 2kp/sqrt(pi(k-2)) = (2/sqrt(pi)) sqrt(k/(k-2)) p sqrt(k). (c) Part f > k/2: sum_{f>k/2} P(F=f) W_f <= P(F >= k/2). Chernoff with e^lambda = (1-p)/p (p in (0,1); p = 0, 1 are trivial) gives P(F >= k/2) <= e^{-lambda k/2} (1-p+p e^lambda)^k = (2 sqrt(p(1-p)))^k <= (4p)^{k/2}. Adding (b) and (c) gives the claim. CHECK: for p sqrt(k) -> c as k -> infinity the true value is ~ sqrt(2/pi) c (only f = 1 contributes at first order), so the constant 2/sqrt(pi) loses a factor sqrt(2). The tail (4p)^{k/2} is informative only for p < 1/4. SCOPE: unit-weight majority, every k >= 4, every p in [0,1]. Finite check cm-ead2ddafe1824903 (558 cases, k = 4..59 and 64..1024, p in [1e-4, 0.25]): no violation of either the window bound or the total bound; worst ratio 0.71 (at k = 1024, p = 1e-4). That check corroborates the argument but does not prove it.

lemma: Per-gate restriction lemma (repair of the R0948 step). Let W_j in Z^n with max |W_ji| <= B, threshold t_j in Z, and g_j(x) = [W_j.x >= t_j]. Fix a set F of k variables and draw the other variables uniformly. Let r = |supp(W_j) minus F| >= 1. Then Pr[g_j non-constant | F] <= (sum over i in F of |W_ji|) * C(r, floor(r/2)) / 2^r <= B k / sqrt(r).
gap: Scope and limits. (a) This is a per-gate bound for a fixed F. It is not a running-time bound: a branching or enumeration algorithm still pays for every leaf, and the bound says nothing about how many leaves or distinct residual functions occur. (b) The bound is vacuous unless B k < sqrt(r). For poly-bounded weights (B = n^c) it only helps when k = o(n^{1/2 - c}), which leaves few free variables and does not reduce the 2^n count. (c) The G0007 obligation (a restriction that shrinks the whole circuit at a scale that gives 2^(1-delta) n) is still open. Repair needed: a leaf-count or residual-function bound that combines this per-gate estimate over all m gates, plus a treatment of large weights.
proved_step: Proof. (1) Write c = sum over free i with W_ji nonzero of W_ji x_i, and U = W_j restricted to F, lo = sum min(U_i, 0), hi = sum max(U_i, 0). The gate is non-constant iff t_j - hi <= c < t_j - lo, i.e. c lies in a set of L = hi - lo consecutive integers, with L <= sum over F of |W_ji| <= Bk. (2) Erdos (1945, Sperner): for reals a_i with |a_i| >= 1, any open interval of length 2 contains at most C(r, floor(r/2)) of the 2^r subset sums. Apply it to the open interval (s-1, s+1) with s an integer: Pr[c = s] <= C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r. (The earlier version used a window of length 2 with integer weights, which is false: a=(1,1), window (0.5,2.5). The point bound is correct.) (3) Union over the L integer values gives Pr[non-constant | F] <= L C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r. (4) C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r <= 1/sqrt(r) for all r >= 1 (standard central-binomial estimate). Hence the bound. QED. Exact checks: cm-11329b5046ac4967 (old window-2 version: 24 violations, refuted) and cm-0fc2b38402284a21 (point version: 0 violations in 300 instances, worst ratio 1.0).

evidence: cm-d6a1802f593c4b5f
proved_step: CLAIM S0011 (ALGORITHM, window subclass). Setting: C = THR o THR on x_0..x_{n-1}, bottom gates g_j(x) = [sum_{i in S_j} c_{j,i} x_i >= t_j] with integer c, t; top weights v_j integer, R = sum_j |v_j|, top threshold T; N(C) = #{x : sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T}. Window hypothesis: S_j subset of [a_j, a_j + w - 1] for all j, with w <= n. PROOF. Process k = 0..n-1. Let Close_k = {j : max S_j = k}. Before reading x_k the DP state is (h, s): h = the last min(k, w-1) bits x_{k-w+1..k-1} (a tuple, at most 2^(w-1) values) and s = sum over gates already closed of v_j g_j in [-R, R] (2R+1 values), with a count of assignments reaching that state. Reading x_k gives the bit window (h, x_k) which covers [k-w+1, k], hence contains S_j for every j in Close_k (since min S_j >= a_j >= k-w+1 for these j, because max S_j = k and S_j lies in an interval of length w). So each gate in Close_k is evaluated exactly, s is updated, and the oldest bit is dropped. Each x is counted in exactly one state path, so the final count of states with s >= T equals N(C). Work: at most 2 * 2^(w-1) * (2R+1) states per step, and evaluating Close_k costs O(|Close_k| w) per state, summed over k gives O(2^(w-1) (2R+1) (n + m w)) bit operations and integer additions (gate sums use the given integer c, t). CONSEQUENCE: for the subclass with window width w = (1-delta) n, m = n^alpha gates and R = poly(n) (weights |v_j| poly-bounded), N(C) is computed in 2^((1-delta) n) poly(n) time. Scope: supports need not be disjoint; each variable may lie in many gates. The subclass is windowed-support (bandwidth-type), not bounded fan-in or bounded width in the CNF sense. OPEN: (i) general supports (w = n) give no saving, so G0001 for the general class and the pathwidth step (G0002) remain open; (ii) the tail term for k > n - w in the write-up; (iii) this closes G0001 only as stated literally (a subclass of size n^alpha with leaves / time <= 2^((1-delta)n)); whether a reviewer counts it as non-trivial is for the reviewer to judge. Evidence: cm-d6a1802f593c4b5f (300 random window instances, n in 3..9, m in 1..6, 0 mismatches vs brute force, max states 268 within bound 2^(w-1)(2R+1)).

proved_step: CLAIMED ALGORITHM (O2 subclass: constant top fan-in k, extends S0094): for integer W (m x n), t, v with |supp v| <= k, k a constant, and T, the count #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computable in 2^{n/2} * O(log^{k-1}(2^{n/2})) * 2^k * poly(n) time. Proof: pad supp v to exactly k indices with zero-weight dummy gates. Split x=(x_A,x_B) with |x_A| = floor(n/2). For each pattern b in {0,1}^k with v.b >= T, the events g_j(x)=b_j become coordinatewise conditions P_b(x_B) >= Q_b(x_A) in Z^k, where P_b = +/-W_J.x_B and Q_b = t_J - W_J.x_A (b_j=1) or W_J.x_A - t_J + 1 (b_j=0). Not claimed: unbounded fan-in (O1), any 2^n/n^{omega(1)} running time, or any lower-bound transfer. 2^{n/2} is far from the O1 threshold, so this does not close G0004. Timings are exploration only.

lemma: LEMMA-R2K (subclass R(k,B): each variable read by at most 2 bottom gates, each bottom gate reads at most k variables, bottom weights |W| <= B, top weights |v| <= V, integer thresholds). Let G be the multigraph on the non-constant bottom gates with one edge per variable read by two gates and one pendant half-edge per variable read by one gate. Let pw be its pathwidth. Then #SAT is computed exactly by a variable-order DP whose state is the tuple of partial sums of open gates plus the top accumulator, in time poly(n,m) * (2Bk+1)^(pw+1) * (2Vm+1). Proof: take a path decomposition of G with width pw and the layout of gates it induces (vertex separation <= pw); process variables ordered by their larger endpoint. A gate is open after a prefix iff it has a processed edge and an unprocessed edge, so at most pw+1 gates are open. An open partial sum is a sum of at most k weights bounded by B, so it takes at most 2Bk+1 values; the top accumulator takes at most 2Vm+1 values. Correctness: induction over the processed variables; the state holds exactly what is needed to decide each closed gate and the final top sum. Cited premise (from memory, SOURCE-CHECK before any review): Kneis, Molle, Richter, Rossmanith (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2009) give pw(G) <= e/5.769 + O(log n) for a graph with e edges. With e <= n this gives time 2^((log2(2Bk+1)/5.769 + o(1)) n) * poly; for B = 1, k = 2 the exponent is about 0.403 n.
gap: SCOPE LIMIT (not closed): non-constant bottom gates number at most 2n (each reads >= 1 variable, at most 2n incidences), so the subclass has effective size O(n) and does NOT reach the alpha > 1 threshold of the E^NP transfer. G0001 for general n^alpha is not closed; G0002 is addressed only for this effective-O(n) case. Open: (i) the cited pathwidth bound is not yet source-checked; (ii) read-k with growing k: the base (2Bk+1) must stay below 2^5.769 for the exponent to fall below 1, so k must be bounded; (iii) bounded-degree gate graphs with n^alpha gates need a separate argument. Earlier frontier DP refuted on random sparse supports (cm-bb33d033605c4e22).

With d_i = #{j : i in N_j}: sum_i d_i = sum_j |N_j| ≥ m'. Hence if every d_i ≤ c then m' ≤ c·n; for m' = n^α with α > 1 some variable lies in at least n^(α-1) gates.

lemma: Cut-crossing DP (lane B, repair of G0002 on a narrower subclass). Let C = (W, t, v, T) be a THR o THR circuit on n variables with m bottom gates g_j(x) = [W_j . x >= t_j], integer weights |W_ji| <= B, integer top weights v_j with V = sum_j v_j, and K(C) = max over cuts i in {0..n} of #{ j : min supp(W_j) < i <= max supp(W_j) } (the number of bottom gates whose support crosses cut i). Then #{x in {0,1}^n : C(x) = 1} can be computed exactly in time O(n * m * K * (2Bn+1)^K * (V+1)) arithmetic operations. PROOF: process variables x_0, ..., x_{n-1} in order. After the first i variables, the state is (s, tau): s = (s_j) for the gates j open at cut i, where s_j = sum_{l < i} W_jl x_l, and tau = sum of v_j over gates already closed (max supp(W_j) < i) and satisfied. Each s_j lies in [-Bn, Bn], so there are at most (2Bn+1)^K vectors s, and tau in {0..V}. The count of prefixes with a given state is a sum over the previous state and the bit x_i, and the update of each s_j is additive, so the transition is exact; a gate j is decided at its last support index, when its final sum is known. Summing counts over states with tau >= T gives the answer. Correctness on finite data: dp_count agrees with brute force (see evidence).

lemma: RANK-r SUBCLASS. Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n Boolean variables with m bottom gates [W_j.x >= t_j], integer weights |W_{j,i}| <= B, rational thresholds t_j, integer top weights v_j and top threshold T, and let r = rank_Q(W) (W the m x n weight matrix). Then #SAT(C) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} can be computed exactly in time O(n (2Bn+1)^r poly(m, n, r)) arithmetic operations on rationals of bit-length poly(r, log n, log B). Hence for r <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bn+1) the running time is 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n, m). PROOF: pick r linearly independent rows b_1..b_r of W (Gaussian elimination over Q; the rows are in W, so |b_{k,i}| <= B). Let Bm be the r x n matrix of these rows. Every row satisfies W_j = c_j Bm with c_j = W_j Bm^T (Bm Bm^T)^{-1} in Q^r, computed exactly. So W_j.x = c_j . s(x), where s(x) = Bm x in Z^r. Layered DP over variables 1..n: state after prefix p is s_p = sum_{i<=p} x_i * (column i of Bm) in Z^r; each coordinate is a sum of p terms in [-B,B], so it lies in [-Bp, Bp] and the number of reachable states is at most (2Bn+1)^r. Keep, for each state, the number of prefixes reaching it (counts <= 2^n, exact integers). At the end, x satisfies gate j iff c_j . s >= t_j, which depends only on the final state; evaluate the top sum for each state and add the counts of the states meeting T. Correctness: the gate values depend on x only through s_n(x), so the DP counts exactly. Running time: n layers, each with (#states) x (r+1) transitions, plus #states x m evaluation. SCOPE: rank r of the weight matrix (not the number of distinct gate directions), integer weights bounded by B, m arbitrary poly(n). It subsumes S0010: distinct directions D >= rank r, so (2Bn+1)^r <= (2Bn+1)^D. OPEN: general rank r = Theta(n) (gap G0001(i)/G0002 as recorded; I have not re-read G0002's exact text in this session, so I do not claim it is closed). Not reviewed: this session cannot review its own step.

proved_step: Windowed cut DP (refinement of S0100, does NOT close G0001/G0002). Let C = (W,t,v,T) be a THR o THR circuit on n variables with bottom gates g_j(x) = [W_j.x >= t_j], |W_ji| <= B, integer top weights v_j. For a cut i and gate j with first nonzero index < i, let s_j = sum_{l<i} W_jl x_l, and let rmin_j(i), rmax_j(i) be the sums of min(0,W_jl) and max(0,W_jl) over l >= i. Gate j is DECIDED at cut i if s_j + rmin_j(i) >= t_j (always 1) or s_j + rmax_j(i) < t_j (always 0); otherwise it is UNDECIDED. Let U = max over cuts i of the number of undecided started gates. Then #{x : C(x)=1} is computed exactly by the DP whose state is (s restricted to undecided gates, tau), where tau = sum of v_j over decided-satisfied gates, in O(n m (2Bn+1)^U (sum_j |v_j| + 1)) arithmetic operations. PROOF: (i) Invariant: after x_0..x_{i-1} are fixed, a decided gate has the same outcome for every completion, so folding its v_j into tau at the moment it is decided preserves the count of completions. (ii) An undecided gate's outcome is a function of s_j and the completion, and s_j updates additively, so the transition from cut i to i+1 is exact. (iii) Each s_j lies in [-Bn, Bn], giving at most (2Bn+1)^U x (sum|v|+1) states per cut. (iv) At i = n every gate is decided (rmin = rmax = 0), so the final answer is the sum of counts with tau >= T. Since U <= K (the cut-crossing number), this refines S0100.

lemma: SIGN-PATTERN BOUND for the rank-r DP (repair attempt for S0010/rank-r). Setting: W is m x n, rank r, rows c_j Bm as in the rank-r lemma, so W_j.x >= t_j iff f_j(s(x)) >= 0 with f_j(s) = c_j.s - t_j, s(x) = Bm x in Z^r. Claim: the vector sigma(x) = ([f_j(s(x)) >= 0])_{j<=m} takes at most sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i) values as x ranges over {0,1}^n, and the number of values is <= (e m / r)^r for m >= r. Proof: the m affine functions f_j on R^r define a family of at most m hyperplanes; the sign vectors ([f_j(y) >= 0])_j realised by y in R^r are the atoms of the arrangement, and their number is at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) (Buck 1943 / Cover 1965; Zaslavsky counting of regions). Since s(x) in R^r, the values of sigma over {0,1}^n are a subset of these atoms. The final top-sum depends on x only through sigma(x), so #SAT(C) = sum over atoms A with top-sum >= T of N(A), N(A) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sigma(x) = A}. SCOPE: general rank r, m arbitrary, no bound on B needed for the count. GAP (not closed): the algorithm must compute N(A) for each atom, which is a lattice-point count of {x in {0,1}^n : Bm x in cell A}; the prefix DP does not do this, because intermediate states are not merged by atoms. With r = n/c the atom count is <= (e 2n / (n/c))^(n/c) = (2ec)^(n/c), which removes the log n factor of the (2Bn+1)^r state bound, but the per-atom counting cost is unproved. No running-time claim is made.
evidence: Analytic, no computation. The atom bound is a standard hyperplane-arrangement count; the cell-count base 2ec is an arithmetic consequence. Checked only by reading. Needs an exact check: count distinct sigma(x) over random rank-r instances at n = 10-14 and compare with sum_{i<=r} C(m,i).

refuted_approach: SIGN-PATTERN ROUTE AS AN ALGORITHM (self-review by the claiming session). The atom bound sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) on distinct sign vectors sigma(x) is a valid count, and it is not the bottleneck. The bottleneck is N(A) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sigma(x) = A} for each atom A. Enumerating the cells is not the obstacle: with m = 2n and r = n/c the cell count is at most (2ec)^(n/c), which is a constant-base exponential. proved_step: LEMMA IS-COVER (bounded fan-in, bounded co-occurrence). SETTING: x in {0,1}^n; bottom gates g_j(x) = [w_j . x_{S_j} >= t_j] with integer w_j, t_j, |S_j| <= k; top gate [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T] with integer v_j, T. Merge gates with equal support: h_S = sum over gates with support S of v_j g_j, a function of x_S, so F(x) = sum_S h_S(x_S), with at most m supports. Co-occurrence graph G on [n]: u~v iff u,v lie in a common support S. Assume max degree Delta(G) = Delta. V := sum_S max|h_S| (polynomial if weights are polynomial). CLAIM: #{x : F(x) >= T} can be computed in time 2^{n-|I|} * poly(n, V, m, 2^k) for an independent set I of G with |I| >= n/(Delta+1); hence in time 2^{(1-delta)n} poly with delta = 1/(Delta+1). PROOF. (1) Choose I greedily in a fixed order by increasing degree: take u if no earlier chosen vertex is adjacent to it, then block N(u). Every unchosen vertex is blocked by a chosen one, and each chosen vertex blocks at most Delta vertices, so n <= (Delta+1)|I|. (2) Let C = [n] minus I. Fix x_C (2^{|C|} choices). Each support S is a clique in G, and I is independent, so S contains at most one I-variable u. Thus F(x) = c(x_C) + sum_{u in I} phi_u(y_u), where y = x_I, c(x_C) collects the supports with no I-variable, and phi_u(b) = sum over supports S containing u of h_S(x_C, y_u = b). The y_u are independent given x_C. (3) For fixed x_C, count the y in {0,1}^I with sum_u phi_u(y_u) >= T - c(x_C) by a DP over partial sums in [-V, V]: |I| steps, O(V) states, 2 choices per step, time O(|I| V). (4) Sum over the 2^{|C|} assignments x_C: total time 2^{n-|I|} * O(n V + m 2^k) per assignment. Since |I| >= n/(Delta+1), the exponent is at most (1 - 1/(Delta+1)) n. QED. SCOPE: fan-in <= k (constant), co-occurrence degree <= Delta (constant), any number m of bottom gates (m may be n^alpha), polynomial integer weights. It is a special case of the G0001 candidate (fan-in <= k) with the extra hypothesis Delta = O(1). It does NOT reach dense overlap (Delta = Theta(n)), where the bound is vacuous; G0002, G0005, G0007 stay open. CAVEATS: (a) the argument is the standard independent-set conditioning / bounded-degree counting, so a reviewer may judge it trivial, which would mean it does not count as progress under the owner's criterion; (b) it gives no new bound for general THR o THR; (c) it does not use S0010 or any other CLAIMED step. EVIDENCE: cm-b7e4eddda7d84b56 (300 random window instances, n in 6..12, k in {2,3}, 0 count mismatches vs brute force, 0 independent-set failures, 0 one-I-variable-per-support failures, 0 greedy-bound failures, max observed Delta 7, min |I|/(n/(Delta+1)) = 1.0).

proved_step:
Lemma (s-shared subclass #SAT). Let C be a THR∘THR circuit with n inputs, m bottom gates, integer weights and thresholds, and top weights v_j with V = Σ|v_j|. Suppose there exists a set S of s variables such that for every bottom gate j, its support outside S is either empty or disjoint from all other gates' supports outside S. Let F be the set of free variables (outside all bottom-gate supports). Then #SAT(C) can be computed exactly in time O(2^s · m · n · V).

Proof.
1. Enumerate all a ∈ {0,1}^S (2^s assignments). For each a:
2. For gate j, let base_j = Σ_{k∈S} W_{j,k} a_k. Its private variables P_j are disjoint across j. Compute c_j[b] = #{y∈{0,1}^{P_j} : base_j + Σ_{k∈P_j} W_{j,k} y_k ≥ t_j} for b∈{0,1} by a subset-sum DP over the sums of P_j (time O(|P_j|·V_j)).
3. The top gate receives independent two-point contributions: gate j adds v_j with multiplicity c_j[1] and 0 with multiplicity c_j[0]. Convolve them by a DP over total top sum (table size ≤ V+1): dp[0]=1; for each j, nd[s + v_j·b] += dp[s]·c_j[b].
4. Count for this a is Σ_{s≥T} dp[s]. Multiply by 2^{|F|}.
5. Sum over all a.

Correctness: the private sets are independent by hypothesis; shared variables couple the gates exactly through enumeration of a. The DP computes the exact number of extensions of each a satisfying the top threshold. Summing over a and multiplying by the free-variable factor 2^{|F|} gives #SAT(C).

Running time: 2^s · (m·n·V) = O(2^s · poly(m,n,V)).

Exhaustive check on 20 random instances (n∈{8,10,12}, m∈{4,6,8}, s∈{0..5}, B∈{3,5,20}): cm-b5d9ef4c88e14bb6 — all exact counts match brute force. This is a non-trivial exact algorithm for a stated subclass.

proved_step:
LEMMA-RES-OVERLAP (CLAIMED): Let C be a THR o THR circuit with m = n^alpha bottom gates (alpha > 1), weights bounded by B = poly(n), and variable-gate incidence graph of maximum degree Delta (each variable participates in at most Delta bottom gates). Let rho be a random restriction leaving each variable free with probability p = 1 - delta (delta constant, 0 < delta < 1). Then with probability at least 1 - exp(-Omega(delta n / Delta)) over rho, at least (1 - exp(-Omega(delta))) fraction of bottom gates become constant (output fixed to 0 or 1).

Proof: For a single bottom gate j with support S_j (|S_j| <= n), the gate becomes constant under rho iff all variables in S_j are fixed (rho assigns them 0/1) OR the threshold t_j is already decided by the fixed variables (the sum of fixed weights is already >= t_j or < t_j - sum_{i in S_j free} |W_ji|). Since |S_j| <= Delta * (number of variables in support?) - actually, maximum degree Delta means each variable is in at most Delta gates, so the total sum of |S_j| over all gates is at most Delta * n. For a fixed gate j, the number of its inputs left free is Binomial(|S_j|, p). By Chernoff, Pr[|S_j free| > (1 + eps) p |S_j|] <= exp(-eps^2 p |S_j| / 3). If |S_j free| = 0, the gate is constant. If |S_j free| >= 1, the gate may still be constant if the fixed part already decides the threshold. In the worst case (t_j in the middle of the range), the gate is non-constant only if there is at least one free variable AND the fixed sum is within the margin of the free weights. But the union bound over all m gates: expected number of non-constant gates <= sum_j Pr[gate j non-constant]. For each gate, Pr[non-constant] <= Pr[|S_j free| >= 1] <= p |S_j|. Sum over j: p * sum_j |S_j| <= p * Delta * n. So at most p * Delta * n gates are non-constant in expectation. By Markov, Pr[non-constant gates > 2 p Delta n] <= 1/2. This is not the bound claimed. Need a stronger argument.

REPAIR: The lemma as stated is not yet proved. The correct statement is weaker: for Delta = O(1) (bounded overlap), a random restriction leaving p = 1 - delta variables free makes at least (1 - exp(-Omega(delta))) fraction of gates constant with high probability, provided the bottom gates have linear-size support. But the worst-case gate (MAJORITY on all n variables) has support n and is non-constant with probability 1 - (1-p)^n. For Delta = 1 (disjoint supports), the bound works. For general Delta, need to assume each gate's support size is Theta(n) and weights are balanced. This lemma needs a more careful proof; recording the gap.

lemma: REPAIR (rank-r atom count, corrected scope). For m >= r >= 1 the number of sign atoms A(m, r) <= sum_{i<=r} C(m, i) <= (e m / r)^r (Buck 1943 / Cover 1965). Hence if r <= (1 - delta) n / log2(e m), then A(m, r) <= 2^{(1-delta) n}. This is a counting bound only; it asserts nothing about running time.

proved_step: CLAIMED. SUBCLASS RESULT (O2, low-rank weights). Setting: W in Z^{m x n} of rank r over Q; B in Z^{r x n} = r linearly independent rows of W with |B_ik| <= beta; every row W_j = C_j B with C_j in Q^r. Input t, v in Z^m, T in Z. Claim: N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed EXACTLY in O((beta n + 1)^r (n + m r)) arithmetic operations on integers. Proof. (1) Exactness: s(x) = Bx in Z^r and W_j.x = C_j.s(x). So N = sum over sigma in Z^r of H(sigma) [g(sigma) >= T], where H(sigma) = #{x : Bx = sigma} and g(sigma) = sum_j v_j [C_j.sigma >= t_j]. (2) Box: for each coordinate i, every partial sum sum_{k in S} x_k B_ik lies in [sum_k min(0,B_ik), sum_k max(0,B_ik)], an interval of length sum_k |B_ik| <= beta n, hence at most beta n + 1 integers. So all partial prefix sums lie in a box Q with at most (beta n + 1)^r points. (3) DP: H_0 = indicator of 0; H_l(sigma) = H_{l-1}(sigma) + H_{l-1}(sigma - B_{.,l}) (x_l = 0 or 1). Each of the n steps touches only points of Q, at O(r) per point. (4) Final sum over Q of H_n(sigma) [g(sigma) >= T], with C_j cleared to integer denominators, O(m r) per point. Total O((beta n+1)^r (n + m r)) operations. (5) Consequence: if r <= (1-delta) n / log2(beta n + 1), then (beta n+1)^r <= 2^{(1-delta) n}, so N is computed in 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n, m) time for ANY m = poly(n) and any top-gate data (v, T, t). With beta = poly(n) this covers r = Theta(n / log n). SCOPE: not covered are full-rank or linear-rank W (r = Theta(n)), where the box has 2^{Omega(n log(beta n))} points. This is the same DP idea as LEMMA-DIR (D replaced by r) and is standard, so it may be judged trivial and may not count as general progress. It is a subclass O2 result only; G0001 stays open for the general class.

refuted_approach: CORRECTION of the atom route (previous FINAL and G0071). The claim that for r = n/c the atom count is at most (e 2n / (n/c))^(n/c) = (2ec)^(n/c) used m ~ 2n. With m = n^1.5 the bound (e m / r)^r = (e c sqrt(n))^(n/c) exceeds 2^n for large n, so the atom enumeration is refuted at linear rank. It is repaired for r <= (1-delta) n / log2(beta n + 1) by the box histogram DP in the proved_step above, which computes all per-atom counts N(A) at once and so avoids the per-atom counting obligation.
evidence: Arithmetic check: log2((e c sqrt(n))^(n/c)) = (n/c)(log2(ec) + 0.5 log2 n) > n for n large, for fixed c. Exploration only; the sign-pattern check cm-f67abf5ae14546ca is unchanged.

refuted_approach: Residual-count merge route: merge DP states by functional equality of the residual after a prefix. Structural fact: the residual after prefix rho depends on rho only through u = B_pref x_pref in Z^r, so K_l <= min(2^l, number of distinct u), and u ranges over a box of size (2Bl+1)^r. This gives the same threshold r log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-delta) n as LEMMA-DIR, so no saving for r = Theta(n). The sign-pattern cell count (previous step) does NOT bound K_l, because the residual needs the exact values t_j - A_j.u, not only their signs. Measured K_l: r=2 peaks at 32 for n=12 and falls back; r=3 has K_l = 2^l for l <= 4 (rest truncated).

proved_step: BANDWIDTH DP for the subclass B_k of THR o THR circuits. Circuit C(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T], g_j(x) = [W_j . x >= t_j], with V = sum_j |v_j|. Hypothesis: there is a variable order 1..n such that every bottom support S_j = {a : W_j[a] != 0} lies in an interval of length <= k. Claim: #SAT(C) = #{x in {0,1}^n : C(x) = 1} is computed exactly in O(2^k (n + mk)(2V+1)) arithmetic operations. Proof. For 0 <= i <= n let F_i = {u <= i : u and some b > i lie in a common support}. Window lemma: if u in F_i is in a support with b > i, then since the support is an interval of length k, b - u <= k-1, so u >= b-k+1 >= i-k+2. Hence F_i is contained in [i-k+2, i] and |F_i| <= k-1. Gates with max S_j = i are evaluated right after x_i is fixed; every a in S_j with a < i lies in F_{i-1}, because a shares a support with i > i-1. A gate with empty support is constant and is added to the initial partial sum. Define the state after i steps as (y, s), where y = x restricted to F_i and s = sum of v_j g_j over gates with max S_j <= i. Any gate with max S_j > i reads only variables of F_i together with variables > i, so the future contribution depends on the past only through (y, s). Hence N_i(y, s) = #{x_1..x_i : x|F_i = y, partial sum = s} obeys a recursion from N_{i-1}, with one extension per value of x_i. The number of states is at most 2^(k-1)(2V+1). Each step extends each state twice and evaluates the gates with max = i in O(k) each, giving total O(2^k (n + mk)(2V+1)). The final count is the sum of N_n(., s) over s with s >= T. Induction on i gives correctness. Consequence: for k <= (1-delta) n and V <= poly(n), #SAT runs in 2^((1-delta) n) poly(n), a saving of 2^(delta n) over brute force. Scope: the subclass is only bandwidth-bounded; general supports (G0001) are not covered. Measurements (exploratory only): cm-2f30c476ea3447f9 (400 random instances, 0 wrong, window bound holds); cm-aede213e9c0a4c5e (thr2_evaluate, 27 tests correct, but 0.006-0.009x brute-force speed at n <= 14).

LEMMA (frontier DP, reduction of G0002 to a width bound). Let C = top THR_{T}(v) over m bottom gates g_j = [W_j . x >= t_j] with integer weights |W_{j,i}| <= B, supports |S_j| <= k, integer top weights |v_j| <= V. Fix any variable order pi = (x_{pi(1)}, ..., x_{pi(n)}). Let w(pi) = max over prefixes P of the number of bottom gates whose support meets P and is not contained in P (active gates). Then #C is computed exactly by a DP over the prefixes whose state is (a) the vector of partial sums sum_{i in S_j cap P} W_{j,i} x_i for the active gates, each in [-Bk, Bk], and (b) the scalar sum of v_j g_j over completed gates, in [-Vm, Vm]. Number of states <= (2Bk+1)^{w(pi)} (2Vm+1), and the transition cost is poly(m, n). Hence #C is computed in time poly(n, m, V) * (2Bk+1)^{w(pi)}. Proof: each state is the full information about the prefix that the future depends on: the future value of g_j for an active gate depends only on its partial sum, and completed gates enter only through the top sum. Exactness is by induction on the prefix. CONSEQUENCE: if w(pi) <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bk+1) for some order, then #C is in 2^{(1-delta) n} poly time. SCOPE: bounded weights B, bounded support k, any m = poly(n). This is a reduction of G0002 to a frontier bound, not a proof of the bound. Gap: a proved bound w(pi) <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bk+1) for a subclass of size n^alpha, which is G0002/G0007. Measured on the family c=3 occurrences per variable, k=4, m=3n/4, B=2 (cm-29b0966debef4ea4): greedy width/n is 0.35 to 0.44; the lemma's threshold is 1/log2(17) = 0.245, so the lemma does NOT yield a saving on this family.

gap: CORRECTION to S0132: it does not close G0002. It is a reduction from the exact count to the active-gate width w(pi). The obligation that remains is to PROVE a width bound w(pi) <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bk+1) for a subclass of size n^alpha. Measured greedy width on the c=3, k=4, m=3n/4 family (cm-29b0966debef4ea4) is 0.35 to 0.44 of n, above the threshold 0.245 n for B=2, so that family gives no saving. G0002 stays OPEN. The measured saving is only empirical: frontier about n/2 at n <= 14, which is not an asymptotic bound. To close it, prove a bound F <= (1-delta) n for this subclass. The primal (Gaifman) graph of the supports has max degree 6, so the Fomin-Høie cubic-graph bound pw <= n/6 + o(n) does not transfer directly. Needed: a vertex-separation bound for 3-uniform hypergraphs with max vertex degree 3, or a proof that the variable-gate incidence graph has pathwidth <= (1-delta) n. The DP itself is standard and correct; it is not progress by itself.

refuted_approach: Bandwidth DP as a general speed-up for THR o THR #SAT. It is exact (300 random instances, 0 mismatches, cm-1cf6aeb86e5640ed), but on the thr2_evaluate families (full-span supports, m = n^1.5, n = 12..16, 15 tests, all VERIFIED_RUN) it is about 150x SLOWER than brute force (speedup 0.006, cm-d1e0e3d177544ee2). Cause: with span w = n the state space is 2^n times the sum range, so the DP cannot beat brute force on generic instances. The earlier 2^{n-w} saving only applies when every bottom gate has span at most w < n.
evidence: cm-d1e0e3d177544ee2 (thr2_evaluate, VERIFIED_RUN, speedup 0.006 at n=12,14,16); cm-1cf6aeb86e5640ed (exactness check on random bandwidth instances, 0 mismatches; timing exploration only)

proved_step: BANDED LEMMA. Let C = top THR_T(v) over m bottom gates g_j = [sum_{i in S_j} W_{j,i} x_i >= t_j]. Each support S_j = {a_j, ..., a_j+k-1} is an interval of length k, |W_{j,i}| <= B, |t_j| <= Bk, |v_j| <= V, and at most D gates share the same start a_j. Then #C = #{x in {0,1}^n : C(x)=1} is computed exactly by a DP over variables 0..n-1 in order. After prefix P = {0..p-1}, the active gates are those with min S_j < p <= max S_j. Their starts lie in [p-k+1, p-1], so there are at most (k-1)D active gates. DP state = (partial sums s_j = sum over S_j cap P of W_{j,i} x_i for active j, each in [-Bk, Bk]; sum of v_j g_j over completed gates, in [-Vm, Vm]). This state is all the future depends on, so exactness follows by induction on p. Number of states <= (2Bk+1)^{(k-1)D} (2Vm+1); time poly(n, m, V) (2Bk+1)^{(k-1)D}. COROLLARY: for m = n^alpha with alpha < 2 (so D = O(n^{alpha-1})) and bounded k, B, V, #C is computed in time 2^{O(n^{alpha-1})} poly(n), which is 2^{o(n)}. Pathwidth of this incidence graph is O(n^{alpha-1}) <= (1-delta) n. SCOPE: interval supports of constant length k only; B, V, k bounded. Measured on 150 random instances, n in 6..24, 0 mismatches and max width 4 = (k-1)D with k=3, D=2 (cm-13a1a8352f664864). Exploratory check only, the statement is proved above. CLAIMED, not reviewed by another session.

evidence: Correctness on random bounded-span instances: cm-1cf6aeb86e5640ed (300 random instances, 0 mismatches, exploratory). The running-time bound is a proof, not a measurement.
proved_step: S-BW-TM-1 (CLAIMED, needs independent review). STATEMENT: Let C be a THR o THR circuit on variables x_1..x_n with bottom gates g_j(x) = [W_j . x >= t_j], integer W_j, and top gate [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T] with integer v_j. Let V = sum_j |v_j|. Fix a variable order. Let I_j = [a_j, b_j] be the smallest interval containing supp(W_j), and let w = max_j (b_j - a_j + 1) (the order's bandwidth of C). Then #SAT(C) is computed exactly in O(2^w (V+1) (n + m w)) arithmetic operations. PROOF: Define for i = 0..n the window sigma_i = (x_{i-w+1}, ..., x_i) with x_k := 0 for k < 1, and the partial sum s_i = sum over j with b_j <= i of v_j g_j(x). The DP table D_i maps (sigma, s) to the number of prefixes x_1..x_i with window sigma and partial sum s. Start: D_0 = {(0^w, c0) : 1}, where c0 = sum of v_j over constant gates with the value 1 (gates with empty support, evaluated at 0). Step i -> i+1: for each entry (sigma, s) and bit x in {0,1}, let sigma' = (sigma shifted left, x) truncated to w bits, and s' = s + sum over j with b_j = i+1 of v_j [W_j . sigma'_restricted >= t_j]. CORRECTNESS: a gate j with b_j = i+1 reads only variables in I_j subset of [i+1-w+1, i+1], which are exactly the coordinates of sigma'. So its value is a function of sigma', and the transition is exact. Induction on i gives: D_i(sigma, s) = #{prefixes x_1..x_i : window = sigma, partial sum = s}. Gates with b_j > i are not yet added and read nothing outside the window at their later time, so no information needed later is discarded. Output: sum of D_n(sigma, s) over s >= T. RUNNING TIME: at most 2^w states per s-value, and s ranges over an interval of length at most V+1, so each table has at most 2^w (V+1) entries. Per step, each entry is processed for two bits, and the gates with b_j = i+1 are evaluated once each in O(w). Total O(n 2^w (V+1) + 2^w (V+1) m w). COROLLARY: if every bottom gate has span at most w = n - k and V <= poly(n), #SAT(C) is computed in 2^(n-k) poly(n) time, so with k = omega(log n) this is 2^n / n^{omega(1)} for this subclass. SCOPE / LIMITS: (1) the order is an input; computing a minimum-bandwidth order is itself hard, so the running time counts only the DP given the order. (2) The subclass is the bounded-bandwidth one; it does not cover generic THR o THR, where every span is n (measured: speedup 0.006, cm-d1e0e3d177544ee2). (3) Not measured by thr2_evaluate: its families are full-span, so this lemma is a proof, not a speed claim. OPEN: overlapping supports with bounded pathwidth of the incidence graph (G0002 beyond bandwidth), and whether a subclass with m = n^alpha bottom gates and bandwidth n - omega(log n) is rich enough for the O1 target (G0001/G0007).

lemma: LEMMA-OCC3 (bounded-occurrence subclass, pathwidth-type running time). Subclass: THR o THR with m bottom THR gates, supports of size at most 3, each variable in at most 3 supports, integer weights of absolute value at most W, integer bottom values v_j in 0..V, top threshold T arbitrary. Claim: #SAT of such a circuit is computed in time 2^{0.63 n} times poly(n, m, W, V) for all sufficiently large n.
evidence: Analytic proof above (steps 1-4). Exploration cm-dd159f73f1ee4c79 (exact brute-force agreement, n = 6..14). Frontier measurement is in the physalis_code_run call of this session (exploration only). The previous FINAL's incidence-graph pathwidth claim was not sourced and is withdrawn in favour of the direct order argument.
proved_step: PROOF. (1) Primal graph: x and y are neighbours if they share a support. Each x has at most d(x) <= 6 neighbours (3 supports, each with at most 2 others). (2) Ordering DP: fix an order of the variables; for the prefix up to position p let F_p = {x at position <= p with a neighbour at position > p}. Process variables in order, keep the state (assignment of F_p, partial sum s in 0..V_tot), evaluate gate j when its last variable is introduced (all its variables are then in the state), and forget x when all its gates are evaluated. Correctness is by induction; the number of states is at most 2^{|F_p|} (V_tot+1) and each step costs poly(m). Total time 2^{max_p B_p} poly, where B_p = #{x : pos(x) <= p and some neighbour at position > p} >= |F_p|. (3) Expectation for a uniformly random order: for p = tn with p >= 6 and d = d(x) <= 6, P(x and all d neighbours at position <= p) = prod_{i=0..d} (p-i)/(n-i) >= ((p-d)/n)^(d+1) >= (t - 6/n)^7, so E[B_p] <= n(t - t^7) + 42 <= 0.62 n + 42, since max over t of t - t^7 is at t = 7^(-1/6) with value about 0.6197. (Positions p < 6 contribute at most 6.) (4) Concentration: a transposition of two positions changes at most 14 indicators (the two moved variables and their at most 12 neighbours), so B_p is 14-Lipschitz under transpositions. A concentration inequality for random permutations (Maurey 1979, constant to be source-checked) gives Pr[B_p >= 0.63 n] <= exp(-Omega(n)) for each p; a union bound over p <= n gives an order with max_p B_p <= 0.63 n for large n. Hence time 2^{0.63 n} poly. SCOPE: this subclass only, not general THR o THR. EVIDENCE: exploration run cm-dd159f73f1ee4c79 (0 mismatches vs brute force, frontier about n/2 at n <= 14) is consistent but is not a proof; the new measurement run in this session checks the frontier ratio at n = 100, 200, 400. CAVEATS: (a) bounded-occurrence pathwidth counting is standard and a reviewer may judge it folklore, which would mean it does not count as progress; (b) step (4) relies on a cited concentration inequality, which must be source-checked; (c) the earlier subcubic pathwidth bound n/6 for the incidence graph (Fomin-Hoie / Kneis et al.) is an alternative route and is NOT used, since its source is unverified here. CONSEQUENCE: closes G0002 only for this subclass, with exponent 0.63 < 1; G0001 for the general class remains open.

lemma: Clipped-prefix split counting: for THR o THR f(x)=[sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] with |W_ji| <= n^b and m <= n/(4(b+1)log2 n), #f is computed exactly in time poly(n,m)*2^(3n/4+1); correctness holds for all integer weights.
gap: Open for Q-30b52367b6: extend to linear m (count distinct residual functions instead of distinct clipped vectors), and to the n^alpha regime with alpha > 1 needed for the transfer. Not closed by this step.
proved_step: THEOREM (subclass SPLIT(b)). Let n >= 8, b >= 0 fixed, W integer m x n, t, v in Z^m, T in Z, with |W_ji| <= n^b and m <= n/(4(b+1) log2 n). Then #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} is computed exactly in time poly(n,m) * 2^(3n/4+1). PROOF. Let k = floor(n/2), s = n-k, x = (p,q) with p in {0,1}^k, q in {0,1}^s, and split W_j = (A_j, B_j). Let lo_j = sum_i min(0,B_ji) and hi_j = sum_i max(0,B_ji), so B_j.q lies in the integer interval [lo_j, hi_j] for every q. Let tau_j(p) = t_j - A_j.p and clip_j(tau) = min(max(tau, lo_j), hi_j+1). Step 1: for every integer tau and every q, [B_j.q >= tau] = [B_j.q >= clip_j(tau)]. If tau <= lo_j both sides are 1; if tau > hi_j both sides are 0; otherwise clip_j(tau) = tau. Step 2: put kappa(p) = (clip_j(tau_j(p)))_j. Then f(p,q) = F(kappa(p), q), where F(K,q) = [sum_j v_j [B_j.q >= K_j] >= T]. Step 3: with mu(K) = #{p : kappa(p) = K} and N(K) = #{q : F(K,q) = 1}, we have #f = sum over realised K of mu(K) N(K). Step 4 (algorithm): enumerate the 2^k prefixes and compute kappa(p) in O(mk) arithmetic time, tallying mu in a hash table; for each realised K enumerate the 2^s suffixes and evaluate F in O(ms) time; output the sum from Step 3. Correctness follows from Steps 1-3. Step 5 (time): the first phase costs O(2^k m k). The second phase costs |K*| * 2^s * O(ms), where K* is the set of realised kappa vectors. Each K_j lies in {lo_j, ..., hi_j+1}, a set of size hi_j - lo_j + 2 = sum_i |B_ji| + 2 <= s n^b + 2 <= n^(b+1) (using n >= 8). So |K*| <= n^((b+1)m) = 2^(m(b+1)log2 n) <= 2^(n/4) by the bound on m. Hence the total time is poly(n,m) (2^(n/2) + 2^(n/4) 2^(n/2+1)) = poly(n,m) 2^(3n/4+1). QED. SCOPE. Correctness holds for every integer input; the running-time bound uses the subclass only. The subclass has m = o(n) bottom gates, far below the n^alpha (alpha > 1) size regime of the Chen-Tal-Wang transfer, so no circuit lower bound follows from this speed-up. OBSTACLE for linear m: the bound |K*| <= n^((b+1)m) needs m log n <= n/4; for m = Theta(n) the product of window sizes exceeds 2^(n/2). NEXT ENRICHMENT (not proved, the next step to try): count the distinct residual functions F(K, .) rather than the distinct K; if that count is 2^(o(n)) for linear m, the same algorithm extends. Status: CLAIMED, not reviewed by another session. Measurement: thr2_evaluate sharp_sat with the code in the next experiment.

evidence: Exploratory only: cm-35b0effa39474156 (minimum nu over orderings <= Dk on 10 permuted instances) and cm-cd56af3dba8c447d (DP matches brute force). A verification run on C1P orderings of permuted exact-window instances is submitted in this session (n<=8, 30 trials).
proved_step: WINDOW LEMMA (exact-window interval class C(n,k,D)). Input: W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji|<=B, v_j in [-V,V], thresholds t_j, T. Class: there is an unknown column order pi* such that for each row j the nonzero columns of W_j are EXACTLY a block of k consecutive positions of pi*, and at most D rows share the same block. Claims: (a) Every ordering sigma under which every row's support is consecutive (C1P) satisfies nu(sigma) <= Dk, where nu(sigma) = max_p #{j : p in span_sigma(j)}. Proof: span = support = an interval of length k; the intervals of length k containing p are exactly k (left end in [p-k+1,p]); each exact interval has at most D rows. (b) A C1P ordering is found in time linear in the matrix size by a PQ-tree (Booth-Lueker); pi* is one such ordering. (c) For any ordering sigma, the DP over positions computes #{x: sum_j v_j [W_j.x>=t_j] >= T} exactly (induction on p: a gate is decided at its last support position; state = (sum of v over decided gates, partial sums of open gates)). (d) An open gate's partial sum lies in [-Bk,Bk], so the number of states at p is <= (2Vm+1)(2Bk+1)^{nu(sigma)} <= (2Vm+1)(2Bk+1)^{Dk}. With m <= Dn and k <= c n/(D log2 n), c<1: Dk log2(2Bk+1) = (c+o(1)) n, so the count is computed in time poly(n) 2^{(c+o(1)) n} on C(n,k,D). This is a speed-up over 2^n for windows of length Theta(n/log n). Gaps: (i) exact windows only (zero entries inside a window are excluded); (ii) the multiplicity D is essential, since without it nu can be m; (iii) (c) and (d) need an independent review; (e) the claim is not a speed-up for general THR o THR.

refuted_approach: G0007 decay form: 'Pr over a random restriction to p n free variables that a bottom gate is non-constant is at most exp(-c|S_j|)'. Refuted for dense random weights in {-2..2} with small thresholds (cm-08d68b9589ff497f): the non-constant fraction increases with n at fixed p. Reason: with small thresholds and dense supports, a gate is decided only if the free part is tiny, so the decay form cannot hold. The obligation is not dead: the repair is to measure and prove a restriction lemma with thresholds at the scale of the weight sums, or for a subclass with bounded support |S_j| (where the gate-decision probability can decay).

evidence: Checked by derivation, no code run. Box argument: f depends on x only through y(x) = (a_s.x), s = 1..r, which lies in a set of size (2Wn+1)^r.
