proved_step: statement: Let W be an integer m-by-n matrix with pairwise disjoint row supports S_j, each |S_j| <= c log_2 n for a fixed constant c. Let t_j,T be arbitrary integers and v_j integers with V=sum_j |v_j| <= n^C for a fixed constant C. The exact number of x in {0,1}^n satisfying sum_j v_j [sum_i W[j,i]x_i >= t_j] >= T is computable in deterministic polynomial time, specifically O(sum_j 2^{|S_j|} + m(V+1)) arithmetic operations. Proof: For each j enumerate the 2^{|S_j|} assignments to S_j and compute c_j, the number satisfying its threshold. Since supports are disjoint, each gate bit is realized by c_j assignments with bit 1 and 2^{|S_j|}-c_j with bit 0; the n-sum_j|S_j| variables outside all supports are free. Maintain D_j(q), the total multiplicity of gate patterns among the first j gates with score q, with D_0(0)=1. Update D_j(q)=(2^{|S_j|}-c_j)D_{j-1}(q)+c_jD_{j-1}(q-v_j). All reachable q lie in [-V,V], so each of m updates costs O(V+1) integer operations. The answer is 2^{n-sum|S_j|} times sum_{q>=T}D_m(q). Each table entry is at most 2^n and has O(n) bits; thus with V<=n^C and 2^{|S_j|}<=n^c, the algorithm has polynomial bit complexity.

statement: Let W be an integer m-by-n matrix with pairwise disjoint row supports S_j, and let t_j,v_j,T be integers. Put k_j=|S_j| and c_j=|{y in {0,1}^{S_j}: sum_{i in S_j}W[j,i]y_i>=t_j}. Define L_j=max(0,-v_j), L=sum_j L_j, and P(z)=product_{j=1}^m ((2^{k_j}-c_j)z^{L_j}+c_jz^{L_j+v_j}). Then the number of x in {0,1}^n satisfying sum_j v_j[sum_i W[j,i]x_i>=t_j]>=T is 2^{n-sum_j k_j} times sum_{e>=T+L}[z^e]P(z).
evidence: For each row j, exactly c_j assignments on S_j make its gate true and 2^{k_j}-c_j make it false. Since the supports are pairwise disjoint, choices across the supports are independent, and the n-sum_j k_j coordinates outside their union are free. In expanding P, selecting the first term for row j represents a false gate and selecting the second represents a true gate. Both exponents are nonnegative by the definition of L_j. For a gate pattern b in {0,1}^m, its resulting exponent is sum_j L_j+sum_j v_j b_j=L+sum_jv_jb_j, and its coefficient is its number of realizing assignments on the supports. Thus its exponent is at least T+L exactly when its score is at least T. Summing those coefficients and multiplying by the number 2^{n-sum_j k_j} of free-coordinate assignments proves the identity. This is a counting identity; it asserts no polynomial running time when the support counts or polynomial convolution are expensive.

statement_start: Let the bipartite incidence graph between variables and bottom gates have connected components C_1,...,C_r, and let each component contain at most c log_2 n variables, for fixed c. Suppose the top weights are integers with V=sum_j |v_j| <= n^C. Then exact #SAT of the THR o THR circuit is computable in deterministic polynomial time.
evidence: For each component, enumerate its at most n^c assignments and compute the induced score distribution. Convolve the component distributions; disjoint component variable sets ensure every full assignment is counted exactly once. Scores lie in [-V,V], so direct convolution costs O(rV^2) arithmetic operations, polynomial since r<=n+m and V<=n^C. Counts have at most n+1 bits. Isolated variables are singleton components.

evidence: Mathematical verification: the polynomial construction correctly encodes the independent choices on disjoint supports. For each gate j, b_j=0 contributes exponent L_j with multiplicity 2^{k_j}-c_j; b_j=1 contributes L_j+v_j with multiplicity c_j. Product over j gives exponent L + sum v_j b_j = L+q. Coefficient sums over patterns with same q. Factor 2^{n-sum k_j} accounts for free variables. Identity is exact and holds for all integer parameters. No counterexample or argument gap found.

Mathematical verification of S0276: (1) Computing each c_j requires enumerating 2^{|S_j|} assignments to its support S_j. Since |S_j| <= c log_2 n, this is <= n^c per gate, and summing over m <= n^alpha gates gives O(m n^c) = poly(n) operations. (2) The DP maintains D_j(q) for q in [-V, V] where V <= n^C. Each of m updates takes O(V) = O(n^C) arithmetic operations. (3) All integer values are bounded by 2^n (multiplicities) and have O(n) bits. (4) The final sum over q >= T takes O(V) time. Total bit complexity is O(m n^c + m n^C) * O(n) = poly(n). The algorithm is correct by S0275's identity. No counterexample or argument gap found.

The identity is mathematically correct. For each row j with disjoint support S_j (|S_j|=k_j), exactly c_j assignments make the bottom gate true and 2^{k_j}-c_j make it false. Since supports are pairwise disjoint, choices across supports are independent, and the n-sum k_j outside variables are free (factor 2^{n-sum k_j}). The generating function P(z) encodes each gate's contribution: selecting first term = gate false (exponent L_j, weight 2^{k_j}-c_j), second term = gate true (exponent L_j+v_j, weight c_j). For a gate pattern b∈{0,1}^m, the total exponent is sum_j L_j + sum_j v_j b_j = L + sum_j v_j b_j. This is ≥ T+L iff sum_j v_j b_j ≥ T. Summing coefficients for e≥T+L counts exactly the satisfying patterns on the supports. Multiplying by 2^{n-sum k_j} gives the full count. No computational claim is made; the identity is exact for all such instances.

The statement is correct. For each component C_i with at most c log_2 n variables, there are at most 2^{c log_2 n} = n^c assignments. For each component, we can enumerate all n^c assignments and compute the induced score distribution (a vector of length at most 2V+1 ≤ 2n^C+1). Since components have disjoint variable sets, the full distribution is the convolution of the component distributions. Direct convolution of r ≤ n+m distributions of length O(n^C) takes O(r n^{2C}) arithmetic operations, which is polynomial in n. Each count has at most n+1 bits (since there are at most 2^n total assignments), so arithmetic is on poly(n)-bit integers. This gives a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for exact #SAT. No computational savings beyond polynomial time is claimed; this is a structural lemma (kind LEMMA) that could be used as a subroutine.

The inequality is false as stated for all m,n. Take m=1,n=4, W=(0,0,0,0), t=0. The single gate is true on every input, so there is exactly 1 pattern; however sum_{i=0}^4 C(1,i)=2 while (e/4)^4<1, contradicting the asserted chain. More generally, when n>m the sum through n is 2^m, while (em/n)^n can be below 1. Thus the VC/Sauer-style bound cannot support the claimed estimate in the m<=n/4 region; it only has the usual useful form when n<=m.

proved_step: statement: For pairwise disjoint supports S_j of sizes k_j, let c_j count assignments on S_j satisfying gate j, and let v_j be arbitrary integers. Put l_j=max(0,-v_j), L=sum_j l_j, and f=n-sum_j k_j. Then the number of x in {0,1}^n satisfying sum_j v_j [gate_j(x)>=t_j]>=T equals 2^f sum_{e>=T+L}[z^e] product_j ((2^{k_j}-c_j)z^{l_j}+c_j z^{l_j+v_j}). Proof: a product term with true-gate set A has exponent sum_j l_j + sum_{j in A}v_j = L+sum_{j in A}v_j and coefficient equal to the number of block assignments realizing that pattern. Both exponents in each factor are nonnegative, so this is an ordinary polynomial. The cutoff e>=T+L is equivalent to sum_{j in A}v_j>=T; unused variables contribute 2^f.

statement: Let S_1,...,S_m be pairwise disjoint supports, k_j=|S_j|, and let gate j be an integer threshold predicate on S_j with integer top weight v_j. Given T, the satisfying-assignment count can be computed in O(sum_j k_j 2^{k_j} + m(V+1)) arithmetic operations, where V=sum_j |v_j|, and O(V+1) coefficient storage, after processing the factors in the signed-weight generating-function identity. Each intermediate coefficient is at most 2^{sum_j k_j}, so has O(n) bits. Proof: enumerate each block to obtain c_j. Let l_j=max(0,-v_j), L=sum_j l_j. The jth factor has terms at exponents l_j and l_j+v_j, both nonnegative and at most |v_j|. Iteratively update the coefficient array by adding (2^{k_j}-c_j) times the old coefficient shifted by l_j and c_j times the old coefficient shifted by l_j+v_j. After all blocks, an exponent e corresponds to top sum e-L; summing e>=T+L and multiplying by 2^f gives the answer. The largest exponent is at most sum_j |v_j|=V. This is pseudo-polynomial in the weights and restricted to disjoint supports.

evidence: For every completed-gate indicator g_j in {0,1}, |sum_j v_j g_j| <= sum_j |v_j|g_j <= S, where S=sum_j |v_j|. Thus the integer score lies in [-S,S] and has at most 2S+1 possible values. This proves only the disputed signed-score coordinate correction. Experiment cm-4291f1feb81e47fb corroborates the range for m<=4 and v_j in [-2,2], but is finite corroboration. I did not verify the separate state-coordinate factor or the full runtime claim.

lemma: Component score-distribution lemma. Let a THR∘THR instance have n Boolean variables, m integer-weighted bottom threshold gates, top weights v_1,...,v_m∈Z, and threshold T∈Z. Form the bipartite incidence graph joining variable x_i to gate j iff its bottom gate depends on x_i. If every connected component contains at most b variables, then its exact #SAT count can be computed in O(m·2^b + m·V·2^b + c·V·2^b) arithmetic operations and O(V) coefficient storage, where V=Σ_j|v_j| and c is the number of components (the last convolution bound may be replaced by O(c·V·2^b)); each integer has at most n+1 bits. In particular, for b=O(log n), V=poly(n), and polynomial input bit lengths, this is polynomial-time. Proof: each gate belongs to exactly one incidence component, since it is a vertex of that graph. For component h, enumerate its 2^{b_h} assignments and compute each gate output and the component score s_h=Σ_{j in h}v_j·[gate_j=1]. Let a_h(s) be the number of component assignments of score s. Distinct components use disjoint variable sets and disjoint gate sets, so a global assignment is uniquely a tuple of component assignments, its top score is Σ_h s_h, and its count is the coefficient distribution obtained by convolving the a_h. Each score lies in [-V,V]; each partial convolution has at most 2V+1 possible scores and coefficients at most 2^n. A direct convolution of a partial distribution with a_h uses O(V·2^{b_h}) operations, since a_h has at most 2^{b_h} nonzero entries. Summing gives O(VΣ_h2^{b_h})≤O(cV2^b). Enumeration costs O(m2^b) gate evaluations up to polynomial representation/evaluation cost. Sum the final coefficients at scores at least T. Coefficients count subsets of at most 2^n assignments, hence have at most n+1 bits. This establishes the exact algorithm and its stated restricted scope; it does not establish a subexponential bound for unrestricted THR∘THR.

proved_step: statement: Component score-distribution convolution lemma. Let V be a finite set of Boolean variables and let g_1,...,g_m: {0,1}^{S_j} -> {0,1} be arbitrary predicates on supports S_j subseteq V; let w_j and T be integers. Form the bipartite incidence graph on V and gate indices, with edges (x,j) iff x in S_j. Let its connected components be C_1,...,C_q, and let V_i and J_i be the variables and gates in component i. Define D_i(s)=|{a in {0,1}^{V_i}: sum_{j in J_i} w_j g_j(a|S_j)=s}|. Then the number of assignments x in {0,1}^V with sum_j w_j g_j(x|S_j)>=T equals sum_{s_1+...+s_q>=T} product_i D_i(s_i). Proof: every gate support lies wholly in one connected component, since each variable in S_j is adjacent to gate j. Thus the total score is the sum of component scores. Every global assignment is uniquely a tuple of component assignments because the V_i partition V. For each such tuple, its global score is the sum of the component scores. Grouping tuples by their scores gives the stated convolution exactly. Isolated variables have no gates and contribute a factor of 2 through D_i(0)=2; empty-support gates are isolated gate vertices and their constant predicate contributes the corresponding fixed score distribution. Computing D_i by enumeration costs O(sum_i 2^{|V_i|} times the total gate-evaluation cost per assignment); convolving score tables is exact, with pseudo-polynomial dependence on the total absolute weight.

proved_step: statement: Lemma (exact #SAT for logarithmic incidence components). Fix constants c,d. Let C be an explicitly represented THR∘THR instance on n Boolean variables with m≤n^d bottom gates. Assume every connected component of its variable/gate incidence graph contains at most c log₂(n+2) variables; all bottom and top integer weights and thresholds have absolute value at most n^d. Then #SAT(C) is computable exactly in polynomial time. Proof: The incidence components partition the variables, and each bottom gate is adjacent only to variables in its own component. For each component i, enumerate its at most 2^{c log₂(n+2)}=(n+2)^c assignments. For each assignment, evaluate its incident bottom gates and record the resulting contribution z to the top weighted sum; aggregate a table A_i[z] counting assignments with contribution z. Each evaluation and table construction takes polynomial time. Since there are at most m gates, each of polynomially bounded weight, every component contribution and every partial sum has absolute value at most m·n^{2d}, a polynomial bound; thus each table has polynomially many possible integer indices. Initialize D_0[0]=1 and iteratively set D_i[t]=Σ_z D_{i−1}[t−z]A_i[z]. By induction, D_i[t] counts exactly the assignments to the first i components whose total top score is t: the induction step partitions those assignments uniquely by their last-component assignment and its contribution z. Therefore #SAT(C)=Σ_{t≥T}D_k[t], where T is the top threshold. There are at most n components and polynomially many score indices, so the convolutions use polynomially many arithmetic operations. Every count is at most 2^n and therefore has at most n+1 bits; exact integer arithmetic is polynomial time. This proves the lemma, including negative weights, empty components, and isolated variables (an isolated variable contributes a two-assignment table at score zero).
